clue.text: I!

wordplay.reading: I, the Roman numeral for one, and also the word for oneself

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, and it is also me, the speaker, whom everyone looks after first

explanation.walkthrough: Two readings meet in a single letter: as a Roman numeral, I is the number 1; as a pronoun, I is me, myself, a person's top priority. The exclamation mark signals the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Number one means oneself, as in looking out for number one, and is also simply the numeral 1.

clue.text: Wrangle online about nasty beast slain by Heracles

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the other word
wrangling twists things about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
mean means nasty, unkind

explanation.surface: An internet argument about some vicious monster from Greek myth.
explanation.walkthrough: Wrangle looks like a verb about arguing, but it signals rearranging, and the rearranged word splits in two to go around the synonym for nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Killing the Nemean lion, whose hide no weapon could pierce, was the first of Heracles's twelve labours.

clue.text: Possibly lead dead male northward

indicators.note: in a down entry, going north means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: the late means the dead
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A dead man being carried northward, possibly in a lead coffin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' marks lead as just one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead is one example of a metal, which is why the clue says possibly.

clue.text: Permanent loss of ten from outside

indicators.note: losing something means it is taken away from the word

parts.note: external means coming from outside
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: Losing ten of something forever, through some outside force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Permanent loss' reads as a phrase, but only Permanent is the definition; the X is removed from EXTERNAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternal means lasting forever, without end, so it is a synonym for permanent.

clue.text: Do better than dilapidated tin house

indicators.note: something dilapidated has fallen apart, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Almost anything would be an improvement on a crumbling tin shack.
explanation.definitionFit: To outshine someone is to surpass them, performing more impressively than they do.

clue.text: Business manager almost captivates woman (assuming she used to be married)

indicators.note: to captivate is to hold captive, so the shortened word holds the next pieces
almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: an exec is an executive, a business manager
W is an abbreviation for woman
if means assuming that

explanation.surface: A business manager charms a woman, presuming she is divorced.
explanation.walkthrough: The parenthesis seems to be an aside, but 'assuming' is a piece of wordplay and the rest of it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An ex-wife is a woman who was formerly married to someone, which the clue's phrase describes.

clue.text: Cook meat with a bit of rice — that's duller

indicators.note: cooking works ingredients into a new form, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: only a small piece of the following word is used, its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of rice

explanation.surface: A cooking tip: meat with a little rice makes a blander dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamer is the comparative of tame, meaning less exciting, so it is a synonym for duller.

clue.text: Break mother's flask

indicators.note: breaking something smashes it into pieces that can be reassembled differently

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A child is told to smash Mum's bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A Thermos is a brand of vacuum flask, now a common name for any insulated bottle.

clue.text: Cake and limeade, mixed atop hollowed-out nectarine

indicators.note: in a down entry, being atop means coming before in the column
mixing stirs the drink's letters into another order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: hollowing out removes the middle, leaving only the two ends

parts.note: the first and last letters of nectarine

explanation.surface: A dessert recipe: cake and a citrus drink, topped with a scooped-out piece of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A madeleine is a small shell-shaped French sponge cake, famous from Proust.

clue.text: Sound of highway traveled

indicators.note: the sound of a word means another word pronounced the same way

parts.note: a highway is a road

explanation.surface: Traffic noise from the road that was driven along.
explanation.definitionFit: Rode is the past tense of ride, so it means travelled on horseback or by vehicle.

clue.text: Dull? Put a dash of Tabasco in meat stew

indicators.note: the dash of sauce goes inside the stewed letters
to stew meat is to cook it into a mess, so its letters are jumbled
a dash is a tiny amount, here the first letter of Tabasco

parts.note: the first letter of Tabasco, the hot pepper sauce

explanation.surface: A cook adds a splash of hot sauce to a bland meat stew.
explanation.walkthrough: MEAT 'stew' gives MATE, and T, 'a dash of' Tabasco, goes 'in' after MAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A matte finish is flat and non-glossy, so matte means lacking shine.

clue.text: Blond we had cruelly kicked around

indicators.note: one word surrounds the other piece

parts.note: to toe something is to kick or nudge it with the toes

indicators.note: something treated cruelly is knocked out of shape, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone confesses that a blond person in their care was bullied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blond we had' reads as one phrase, but Blond stands alone as the definition. TOED wraps a rearrangement of WE HAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Towheaded means having very pale, flaxen hair, like the colour of tow fibre, so it describes a blond person.

clue.text: Spent a hefty mil, unwisely, to produce a TV sitcom

parts.note: all in is a colloquial way to say exhausted, spent

indicators.note: money spent unwisely is thrown about, so these letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, short for a million

explanation.surface: A TV studio blew a fortune foolishly on making a sitcom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spent' is not the anagram fodder but a synonym: ALL IN. 'unwisely' then rearranges A HEFTY MIL into THEFAMILY.
explanation.definitionFit: All in the Family was a groundbreaking 1970s American television situation comedy starring Archie Bunker.

clue.text: Attempt at remembering guys not in story

parts.note: guys are men

indicators.note: one word is placed inside another

parts.note: a tale is a story
taken as written

explanation.surface: Trying to recall a story, but the men in it are missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not in story' reads as the men being absent from the tale, but the little word is itself a piece placed inside the story.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a mental note is deliberately fixing something in your mind so as to remember it later.

clue.text: Perennial half-lights hiding criminal

indicators.note: the outer piece conceals another word within it
half of the word is dropped, keeping only the front three of six letters

parts.note: taken as written, before it is halved
a felon is someone guilty of a serious crime

explanation.surface: A gardening puzzle: a perennial plant in the half-light concealing a burglar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perennial' suggests a plant, but here it is an adjective. LIG, the first half of LIGHTS, holds FELON.
explanation.definitionFit: Perennial means lasting or recurring year after year, so lasting through a whole life is a synonym.

clue.text: Marvelous soft drink's idiosyncrasy

parts.note: Fanta is a brand of fizzy orange soft drink
a tic is a habitual quirk or mannerism

explanation.surface: Praise for a fizzy drink and its quirky character.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantastic means extraordinarily good, wonderful, a synonym for marvelous.

clue.text: Be ambitious and misinterpret praise

indicators.note: misreading the word gets its letters in the wrong order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to a climber: aim high, and don't take flattery at face value.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire is to have ambition, to aim at something higher, which is being ambitious.

clue.text: It may be a first course in rioting with a revolutionary

definitions.text: It may be a first course

indicators.note: a revolution turns things around, so the letters are turned into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: A first lesson in street protest, led by a firebrand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like a noun for a rebel, but here it signals rearranging. The 'with' just joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigatoni is a tube-shaped pasta, and in an Italian meal pasta is often served as the primo, the first course.

clue.text: Flowery lecture about nation's origin

indicators.note: the verb goes around the other piece

parts.note: to orate is to lecture or speechify

indicators.note: the origin of a word is where it starts, its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of nation

explanation.surface: A florid speech on how the country was founded.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornate means elaborately decorated, and flowery language is ornate in style.

clue.text: Looking back, clear up Mets' property — it involves a batter

indicators.note: looking back means reading the letters from right to left
the answer is the property of the words before it, held within them

parts.note: reading backwards through these words

explanation.surface: A baseball story: in hindsight, the New York Mets should tidy their ballpark.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mets are a New York baseball team, so 'batter' wants to be a hitter; here it is the coating for fried food.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempura is a Japanese dish of seafood or vegetables fried in a light batter.

clue.text: Careful when speaking of record concerning Spielberg movie

parts.note: a record is a disc
re means concerning, as in a memo heading
Steven Spielberg directed E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial

explanation.surface: Someone choosing words carefully while talking about a Spielberg film recording.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When speaking' looks like a signal that the answer sounds like something, but it belongs to the definition: tactful in what you say.
explanation.definitionFit: Being discreet means keeping confidences and choosing words tactfully, which is being careful in speech.

clue.text: Fishkill's handwritten books

parts.note: read as two words, fish is cod and to kill is to ice, slang for murder
the apostrophe-s supplies a plain S

explanation.surface: A New York town called Fishkill owns some old manuscripts.
explanation.walkthrough: Fishkill is a town in New York State; split it into Fish and kill to get COD and ICE, and the 's adds S.
explanation.definitionFit: Codices are ancient manuscript volumes, bound handwritten books rather than scrolls.

clue.text: Wall Street figure losing head in conversation with TV journalist

indicators.note: spoken aloud, the shortened word sounds like the answer

parts.note: a banker is a typical Wall Street figure; losing its head, the first letter, leaves anker

explanation.surface: A financier loses their head while talking with a news presenter.
explanation.walkthrough: Wall Street is New York's financial district. BANKER minus its head gives ANKER, which 'in conversation' sounds like the newsreader's title.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchor is the main presenter of a television news programme, who ties the broadcast together.

clue.text: Marsupial's unusual stamina and villainy

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary arrangement, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: villainy is wickedness, or evil

explanation.surface: A creature is noted for its uncommon endurance and its wickedness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges STAMINA and AND into TASMANIAND; the 's is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tasmanian devil is a carnivorous marsupial found only on the Australian island of Tasmania.

clue.text: A fielder's item nearly heading upriver

definitions.note: the definition proper is river; its 'up' does double duty with heading as the reversal signal

indicators.note: heading up, in a down entry, means travelling toward the top, so the letters read from bottom to top
nearly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
a baseball fielder wears a glove

explanation.surface: A baseball fielder's mitt drifts nearly to the top of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading' looks like a noun, but 'heading up' belongs together as the instruction, leaving 'river' alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Volga is Europe's longest river, flowing through Russia to the Caspian Sea.

clue.text: Vomit beneath small bench

indicators.note: in a down entry, being beneath means coming after in the column

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a pew is a church bench

explanation.surface: Someone is sick under a little bench.
explanation.definitionFit: To spew is to vomit, to throw up forcefully.

clue.text: Oh, picture strange theatrical 6 Across

indicators.note: strange suggests something out of its normal order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at an odd-looking photograph from the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 Across is TAMER: Petruchio is the man who woos and tames Katherina in Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew.
explanation.definitionFit: Petruchio is the shrew's tamer in a Shakespeare comedy, so he is a stage tamer.

clue.text: Musical instrument found in rear half of presidential home

indicators.note: only the back half of the name is kept, the front half dropped

parts.note: Monticello is Thomas Jefferson's house in Virginia

explanation.surface: A musical instrument turns up in a back room of a president's house.
explanation.walkthrough: The presidential home is not the White House but Jefferson's estate, whose ten-letter name splits neatly in two.
explanation.definitionFit: The cello is a large bowed string instrument of the violin family.

clue.text: Wherein individual covens could affiliate, primarily!

definitions.text: Wherein individual covens could affiliate, primarily!

indicators.note: primarily points to what comes first in each word

parts.note: the first letters of these five words

explanation.surface: A description of a religion in which separate witches' groups may join together.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition, and the exclamation mark flags that.
explanation.definitionFit: Wicca is a modern pagan witchcraft religion whose members gather in small groups called covens.

clue.text: Bring back to power, elected instead of Democrat as part of a Republican area

indicators.note: the elected letters stand in the place of the Democrat's letter

parts.note: a red state is a US state that votes Republican, red being that party's colour
a winning candidate is in, elected

explanation.surface: An elected official replaces a Democrat in a Republican stronghold.
explanation.walkthrough: In US politics Republican states are red and Democratic ones blue; 'instead of' swaps the D of RED STATE for IN.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinstate is to restore someone to a former position or office, putting them back in power.
